contents_mass.source: racing_game PR #22 (owner 2026-10-16: fuel and N2O bottle contents count in the car's mass, live as they are used): the chassis body carries the fuel tank and N2O bottle contents on top of its dry mass, updated whenever they moved by 0.1 kg [AS] (about 5 s of cruise or under 1 s at full throttle).

name: car_fairheaven_lt80
source: data/vehicles/car_sedan_rwd.json with the wheel positions and tyre size matched to the imported model data/models/imported/fairheaven_lt80/fairheaven_lt80.glb (tools/carimport): wheelbase 2.652 m (front axle 1.326 m ahead of the CoG, the base car's CoG fraction kept), track front 1.464 m / rear 1.464 m, tyre belted 205/60 R15 (model wheel radius 0.303 m). Everything else is the base file's. Base source: Reference RWD variant of data/vehicles/car_sedan.json (owner request 2026-09-25: FWD/RWD/AWD reference cars as simple baselines for the drivetrain implementation; car_sedan.json itself stays the FWD reference and is NOT modified). Same body, mass (1500 kg), tyres (data/tyres/passenger_car_225_45r17.json), engine (data/engines/i4_2l_na.json), clutch, gearbox (data/gearboxes/sedan_6mt.json), final drive (open differential 4.06, efficiency 0.97 - inside both the typical FWD 3.9-4.4 and RWD 3.4-4.1 ranges for a 2.0 L engine of this output), brakes, aero and driver aids as car_sedan.json - see that file's own source field for every one of those numbers. Differences: (1) the differential feeds RL/RR instead of FL/FR (front hubs undriven, World::wheel_is_driven); (2) static split symmetric 50/50 (a front-engine RWD sedan is conventionally close to 50/50, Genta 'Motor Vehicle Dynamics' ch. 1), so the wheel attachment_local x sits on data/models/car_sedan/car_sedan.rig.json's own susp_* pivots (front x=+1.35 m, rear x=-1.35 m, wheelbase 2.70 m) and the chassis box origin (= mass centre) is at mid-wheelbase. Corner static load 1500*9.81/4 = 3678.75 N (corner mass 375 kg); spring_rate = 3678.75/0.06 = 61312.5 N/m on all four corners (static compression 1/3 of travel_max 0.18 m); damper bump c = 2*0.35*sqrt(61312.5*375) = 3356.5 rounded to 3400 N*s/m (~0.35 damping ratio, Milliken 'Race Car Vehicle Dynamics' ch. 16), rebound 5000 (bump:rebound 25/17, as car_sedan.json). Anti-roll-bar rates unchanged (front 15000, rear 10000 N/m). The auto-clutch/auto-blip tuning was measured on the FWD car; it is drivetrain-generic and kept as-is for this baseline. Racing_game-owned copy (physics_sim is read-only from this repo): identical to external/physics_sim's data/vehicles/car_sedan_rwd.json except (1) every relative file reference points back into external/physics_sim/data/ (this file lives in racing_game/data/vehicles/), and (2) engine garage G1 added a fuel_tank component (E5, 60 L = 44.99 kg capacity at 749.8 kg/m3, initial 48 L = 35.99 kg [AS], the hyper car's 75 L / 60 L ratio kept) and the engine.fuel fluid link, so the garage can offer the fuel choice (D1) on every catalog car. Engine thermal model (2026-10-12, owner decision: every game car has one): names external/physics_sim/data/cooling_systems/sedan.json (the passenger-car class radiator and fan) and starts warm (engine_thermal_start, coolant 91 C, oil 95 C); the engine file supplies the engine side via default_thermal. Tyres (2026-10-13, universal tyres): no tyre files - each wheel carries a tyre_spec (compound + width/aspect/rim) that rg::load_vehicle builds in memory from data/tyres/families.json (tyre_families); a raw ps::io::load_vehicle_json of this file is rejected (physics_sim 6c5bb87: a wheel without a tyre is a load error); rg::load_vehicle injects the tyres through VehicleLoadOptions::tyres.
